Will verify with a real prompt after.

CONFIRMED FIX #1, with a direct unit test against the real file (not just reading code): Echo.js's read_item() only ever matched the retired {at:'content',add:{...}} line shape. Every live prompt since the 2026-10-03 'no at, no dots' wire-format change writes {content:{add:{...}}} instead, so read_item() returned null for every single prompt today, heard() hit `if (!item?.text) return;` and silently gave up - zero errors, zero log lines, exactly what was observed. Patched to accept both shapes (same one-release compat window page_tools.js's own replay() already keeps); ran the fixed logic directly against public/framework/ai/2026/10/02/session-361c4d18/page.jsonl by hand and confirmed it now finds the real item correctly.

SECOND, DEEPER BREAK found after restarting+retriggering twice more with the fix live: added a temporary this.servex.say() as literally the first line of heard() (before any other check) to prove whether the handler is entered at all. Restarted Servex (confirmed clean boot, no startup error, via sustain.log), re-POSTed /log/echo for the still-raw prompt 41b5b67a, got {ok:true} back from the route - and the diagnostic say() never fired. Checked GET /log/servex across the whole post-restart window: zero 'echo:' lines, not even the loop-guard refusal message. This means Echo's own 'append' event listener (Servex.log.on('append', ...), attached in install()->listen()) is not receiving the event at all for name 'echo', even though the SAME route's own code (Servex.Log.append()) emits ('append', name, entry) synchronously right before answering ok:true. Both Echo.install() and the /log/echo route are individually correct by inspection; the break is in the wiring between them, which is Servex.js/Log.js core infra outside this task's /framework/ai/2026-10-03/prompts-live/ fence.
